subject: Dedicated capacity migration: governance & sizing escort plan
messages:
From: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Hayes <d.hayes@riverside.ai>, Riverside Infra <infra-team@riverside.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity migration kickoff: governance & sizing escort plan

Danielle / Infra team,

Thanks again for committing to Dedicated capacity for Q3. Attached is our initial sizing workbook (riverside-sizing-v2.xlsx) and a short governance checklist that maps validation gates to owners. The goal here is to align on:

- Finalized peak RPS and p50/p95 latency targets per model variant
- A pre-cutover dry run date and the acceptance criteria we’ll use
- Escalation and rollback thresholds (cost + latency + error rate)

Proposed high-level timeline (subject to your confirmation):
- Wed 05/22: Redwood sends annotated sizing and test harness (done)
- Mon 05/29: Dry-run in staging (2h window)
- Tue 05/30: Final swap rehearsal + config freeze
- Thu 06/01: Production switch (2h maintenance window)

Can you confirm that Infra can provide a staging pool with identical GPU class and network segmentation for the dry run on 05/29? Also call out any capacity constraints we should be aware of.

Attachments: riverside-sizing-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), governance-checklist.pdf (doc), dryrun-runbook.md (runbook)

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime
From: Danielle Hayes <d.hayes@riverside.ai>
To: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Riverside Infra <infra-team@riverside.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity migration kickoff: governance & sizing escort plan

Priya,

Thanks — received the workbook and checklist. Quick answers:

- We can stand up a staging pool with the same A100-80GB profile but only 8 GPUs available on 05/29 (we currently have a maintenance window on 05/28). That means we'll need to run the dry run with reduced concurrency unless you can simulate load against a subset.
- Network segmentation can mirror prod for egress and VPC peering; we’ll need a short firewall rule change (we can do that during the rehearsal).
- No procurement blockers aside from ephemeral quota for extra IPs; I’ve opened a ticket with infra and CC’d them.

We’d like to see the exact traffic shaping you intend to run in the dry run so we can ensure the KV cache priming matches. Can Marcus share the harness steps?

—Danielle
Director, Platform Engineering
Riverside AI
From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Hayes <d.hayes@riverside.ai>, priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity migration kickoff: governance & sizing escort plan

Thanks Danielle — short note on the harness and priming approach.

We’ll run a 90-minute dry-run that exercises:
1) Cold-start ramps (65% of expected peak RPS) to validate model load times and KV cache behavior
2) A 20-minute sustained peak window at 30% concurrency to validate steady-state throughput
3) Two short burst tests (2 x 2m) at 110% of expected RPS to validate autoscaling and throttling policies

We will produce these artifacts for your team before the dry run:
- load_profile.json (shapes for each replayed workload)
- kv_primer_steps.txt (ordered prompt sets to warm caches)
- acceptance_metrics.md (p50/p95 expected bands, error budget)

If you can stand up 8 GPUs we can run scaled-down concurrency and then normalize metrics to project to full fleet; we’ll call out confidence intervals in the acceptance doc.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: governance owners & guardrails for Riverside migration

Team — internal note for the migration POAM (plan of action):

Open items assigned:
- Monica: coordinate billing ledger tag + cost cap guardrail with Finance; request temporary credit hold if projected delta > 18% weekly
- Marcus: produce load_profile.json and kv_primer_steps.txt by 05/26 EOD
- Aditya: prepare binary-compat and quantization smoke tests for the customer model artifacts; run on a single node on 05/27
- Priya: confirm customer DR window & finalize change control doc (DocuSign link to follow)

Rollback conditions (proposed):
- If p95 latency exceeds baseline + 200ms for 3 consecutive sample intervals (2m) during steady-state, trigger immediate fallback to hosted variant
- If error rate (5xx + model failures) > 1.5% sustained for 10m, abort and revert routing
- If cost run-rate increases beyond 25% of committed estimate during rehearsal, pause and investigate with Finance

I’ll assemble these into the governance-checklist.pdf and tag owners. Keep notes tight; we’ll present this to Riverside on 05/26 sync.

—Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Danielle Hayes <d.hayes@riverside.ai>
To: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Riverside Infra <infra-team@riverside.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2028 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity migration kickoff: governance & sizing escort plan

Priya/Team,

That plan looks sound. A few clarifications before the 05/26 sync:

- We accept the reduced concurrency approach for the dry run but would like a calibrated projection method documented (how you normalize metrics from 8 GPUs -> 32 GPUs). Please put the normalization math in acceptance_metrics.md.
- On rollback: we want an additional constraint — if model quality checks (nDCG / intent accuracy for our key prompts) drop by >3% vs hosted baseline during the dry run, we’d like routing to switch to hosted immediately. Can Aditya own model-quality smoke tests?
- Our compliance lead needs the change-control doc to include a data retention clause for staged logs (30 days) and encryption at rest for staging volumes.

We can confirm firewall change windows: 05/29 10:00–12:00 PT. Staging pool will be available 05/29 in the morning.

Thanks,
Danielle
From: priya_natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Hayes <d.hayes@riverside.ai>, Riverside Infra <infra-team@riverside.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity migration kickoff: governance & sizing escort plan

Quick status after internal run-through this morning and ahead of tonight’s pre-cutover rehearsal: 

- Marcus uploaded load_profile.json and acceptance_metrics.md to the shared drive link. Normalization math is in section 2.1 and includes confidence intervals.
- Aditya completed the quality smoke tests; results: intent accuracy delta = -0.8% vs hosted baseline (within our +/–3% guardrail). He attached smoke test logs in the runbook.
- Monica confirmed Finance will enable a temporary cost cap and his team will send the invoice adjustment PO by 06/03 if we hit the committed threshold.

Plan for tonight (05/30) — pre-cutover rehearsal:
- 20:00 PT: config freeze and final artifact push
- 20:30–21:30 PT: rehearsal window (following dry-run plan but with final routing rules)
- 21:45 PT: short retrospective and go/no-go decision for full swap on 06/01

Please dial into the rehearsal bridge (Zoom link in the drive). Infra — please confirm you’ll be standing by for firewall changes and will have a single on-call for quick revert of routing if needed.

See you on the call,
Priya

Attachments referenced: riverside-sizing-v2.xlsx, governance-checklist.pdf, dryrun-runbook.md
